problems.title: Why Do Electrons Form Cooper Pairs?
problems.statement: The superconducting energy gap is Delta = 1.5 meV. Calculate the pair-breaking energy 2Delta in meV.
problems.solution: A Cooper pair must supply twice the gap energy, so 2Delta = 2(1.5) = 3 meV.

problems.title: The Effective Electron–Electron Attraction
problems.statement: Two electrons exchange a phonon with energy 8 meV. If the effective attraction is 25% of this energy, what is the attraction energy in meV?
problems.solution: The attraction energy is 0.25 x 8 meV = 2 meV.

problems.title: The Superconducting Energy Gap
problems.statement: At zero temperature, a BCS superconductor has critical temperature Tc = 10 K. Using Delta(0) = 1.764 kB Tc and kB = 0.08617 meV/K, calculate Delta(0) in meV.

problems.title: The Density of States Near the Gap
problems.statement: For a normal-state density of states N0 = 4 states/eV, the BCS density of states at E = 2Delta is N(E) = N0 E/sqrt(E^2 - Delta^2). Calculate N(E) in states/eV.
problems.solution: Set Delta = 1 and E = 2: N(E) = 4(2)/sqrt(4 - 1) = 4.619 states/eV.

problems.title: Constructing the BCS Ground State
problems.statement: For one momentum state, the BCS coherence factors satisfy u^2 + v^2 = 1. If v^2 = 0.36, calculate u.

problems.title: The BCS Gap Equation
problems.statement: In a simplified gap equation, Delta = 2 hbar omegaD exp(-1/(N0V)). If hbar omegaD = 10 meV and N0V = 0.5, calculate Delta in meV.

problems.title: Calculating the Critical Temperature
problems.statement: A superconductor has zero-temperature gap Delta(0) = 2.0 meV. Using Delta(0) = 1.764 kB Tc with kB = 0.08617 meV/K, calculate Tc in kelvin.

problems.title: The BCS Coherence Length
problems.statement: The BCS coherence length is xi0 = hbar vF/(pi Delta). If hbar vF = 1.0 x 10^-28 J m and Delta = 2.0 meV = 3.204 x 10^-22 J, calculate xi0 in nm.

problems.title: The Isotope Effect
problems.statement: The isotope effect predicts Tc proportional to M^(-1/2). If Tc = 12 K for isotope mass M = 100, calculate Tc for M = 144 in kelvin.

problems.title: BCS Theory Challenge
problems.statement: A BCS superconductor has Tc = 20 K. Using the weak-coupling ratio 2Delta/(kB Tc) = 3.528 and kB = 0.08617 meV/K, calculate Delta in meV.
